seoTitle: How to Insert a Watermark in Google Docs (2026)
metaDescription: The watermark option moved in Google Docs — here's how to quickly find it and insert a text (Draft) or logo image watermark properly.
intro: Google Docs recently relocated its watermark option, leaving many users unable to find the feature where they expect it. This guide shows two reliable ways to access the watermark tool, including a fast keyboard shortcut, and walks through formatting both text and logo image watermarks.

steps.heading: Understand why the watermark option seems missing
steps.body: Google moved the watermark tool from its previous location in the Insert menu, which is why long-time users often can't find it right away.

steps.heading: Find the watermark tool using the Insert menu
steps.body: Look under the updated Insert menu location where Google now tucks the watermark option, since it hasn't been removed entirely, just relocated.

steps.heading: Use the keyboard shortcut
steps.body: A quick keyboard shortcut can jump straight to the watermark tool without navigating through menus, saving time if you add watermarks often.

steps.heading: Insert and format a text watermark
steps.body: Type in your desired text, such as 'DRAFT,' and adjust its font, size, and transparency so it displays clearly across the page without overwhelming the content.

steps.heading: Insert and format a logo image watermark
steps.body: Upload your logo image as the watermark and adjust its scaling and transparency so it fits appropriately on the page.

faq.question: Why can't I find the watermark option in Google Docs anymore?
faq.answer: Google relocated the watermark feature from its previous spot in the Insert menu, so it's still available but not where long-time users expect it.

faq.question: Is there a shortcut to add a watermark faster?
faq.answer: Yes, Google Docs supports a keyboard shortcut that jumps directly to the watermark tool without navigating multiple menus.

faq.question: Can I use both a text and image watermark at once?
faq.answer: Google Docs' watermark tool typically supports one watermark type at a time, so you'll need to choose either the text or image version.

faq.question: Does the watermark show when I export to PDF?
faq.answer: Yes, watermarks added through this tool typically carry over when the document is downloaded or exported as a PDF.
